fields.meta_title: Safety Survey Questions, Examples, and Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a safety survey from a prompt, with example questions, answers saved by shift or site, and each result sent to the manager who owns it.
fields.h1: Build a Safety Survey That Sends Each Manager Their Own Results
fields.hero_description: Build a safety survey that saves every answer by shift or site in a database you own and alerts the manager in charge.
fields.features_subheading: Six parts of the survey, covering how the questions get written, where answers are stored, and who hears about a problem.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from your worksite

Describe the work and who will answer it. Emergent drafts the questions, pairing agree scales with open boxes, and you reword any question with a follow-up prompt in plain English.
fields.feature_2:
Answers saved by shift, never by name

Each answer is saved with the site and shift it came from, in a database you own. The survey asks for no name, and a group score stays hidden until 5 people in it have answered.
fields.feature_3:
Walkthroughs answered on a phone

Supervisors walk the floor with the checklist open on a phone and answer yes or no for every item on it. Any No opens a corrective task with an owner and a due date attached.
fields.feature_4:
A floor for every question

Set the lowest score each question may reach. When a shift or unit drops under it, the safety manager gets a Slack or email alert with the score and every comment behind it.
fields.feature_5:
Every employee, no response cap

Emergent puts no cap on survey responses. Survey all 900 people across four sites every quarter on one plan, and send reminders only to the shifts where few people have answered.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Put the survey on a custom domain, which Emergent includes and charges in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it after the survey closes.

fields.tab_content_1:
On stopping an unsafe job, night shift scores 2.4

Every quarter, pickers and loaders at the Merced distribution center rate statements out of 5, with no name field. One reads: I can stop an unsafe job without getting blamed. Night shift averaged 2.4 across 23 answers, against 4.1 on days. Any shift under 3.0 goes to the site safety manager, Joelle Tremblay.
fields.tab_content_2:
One unit report, its three lowest statements first

Twice a year, nurses and aides on each hospital unit rate the same safety culture statements. On 6 North, 14 of 34 agreed that staff speak up when they see something that could harm a patient. Nadia Stanhope, the unit manager, gets a report on 6 North alone, with its three lowest statements first.
fields.tab_content_3:
A missing guardrail becomes a task due in 24 hours

On Fridays, the foreman at the Pinegrove Avenue site walks each floor with a 15-item checklist on his phone. On level 3, item 7 asks if guardrails are in place on open edges. He answered No, which opened a task for the superintendent, Owen Lachance, due in 24 hours. It closes when a recheck answers Yes.
fields.tab_content_4:
The same question, asked before and after a route cap

Each quarter, delivery drivers answer one question in the same words: I have enough time to make my stops without rushing. January averaged 2.7 out of 5. In February, the fleet manager capped routes at 120 stops. In April, 58 drivers answered and the average reached 3.8. He sees both rounds on one chart.

fields.howto_title: How to Plan and Run a Safety Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a safety survey that people answer honestly and that gives each result a manager who acts on it.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Tie every question to a decision
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask about one thing per question
fields.howto_step_1_des: A perception survey asks workers how safe they feel and whether they can raise a concern. A walkthrough checklist records what a supervisor sees on the floor. Pick one per survey, because opinion statements mixed with yes-or-no inspection items muddy both sets of results.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Before writing questions, list the decisions the results could change, such as which site gets new lighting or whether night shift needs a second lead. Cut any question that feeds none of them. A shorter survey is easier to finish on a 15-minute break.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A statement like my supervisor and my crew both take safety seriously asks about two groups at once. Pew Research Center says such double-barreled questions are difficult for respondents to answer and often lead to responses that are difficult to interpret. Split it in two.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Leave out names and employee IDs, and show a group score only once 5 or more of its members answer. On a night crew of 6, a smaller cutoff would let a supervisor work out who said what.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide who acts on each kind of result: the site safety manager for shift scores, the superintendent for walkthrough items, a unit manager for their own unit. Then set the score that triggers an alert, such as any average under 3.0, and name who receives it.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with a fake shift
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before launch, submit 5 test answers as a made-up night shift, with one score under the alert line. Check that the group score appears only after the fifth answer and that the alert reaches the safety manager with the comments. Then delete the test rows.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Report back and keep the wording
fields.howto_step_7_des: Within a month of closing, tell crews what changed because of their answers, such as a forklift aisle moved away from a blind corner. Keep the core statements word for word each round, since Pew notes that even small wording differences can substantially affect the answers people provide.

faq_plan.q: What is a fire safety survey?
faq_plan.ref: what is a fire safety survey
faq_plan.a: A fire safety survey is a walk-through of a home or building to find fire hazards before they start a fire. In Rockford, Illinois, firefighters walk through the home with the resident to identify hazards and check that each smoke detector works properly.

faq_plan.q: How do you create a safety survey report?
faq_plan.ref: how to create a safety survey report
faq_plan.a: Open the report with who answered: the count per site or shift and the dates the survey ran. Then list the lowest-scoring questions with their comments, and give each one a corrective action with an owner and a target date. Emergent's AI survey builder can build the report page from the same prompt as the survey, reading from the response table.

faq_plan.q: What is a culture of safety survey?
faq_plan.ref: what is a culture of safety survey
faq_plan.a: A culture of safety survey asks staff how their workplace treats safety, instead of counting incidents: whether they can report a mistake without blame, and whether managers act on concerns. In healthcare, the AHRQ Surveys on Patient Safety Culture ask staff about the extent to which their organizational culture supports patient safety. Run it anonymously each year.

faq_plan.q: What is a home safety survey?
faq_plan.ref: what is a home safety survey
faq_plan.a: A home safety survey is a visit in which a firefighter or other trained visitor checks a house for hazards. Gulf Shores Fire Rescue designs its surveys to identify fire and life-safety hazards such as slipping, tripping, and cooking, and its firefighters can provide written recommendations. Workplace versions ask people instead, closer to an employee engagement survey.

faq_plan.q: What is a life safety survey?
faq_plan.ref: what is a life safety survey
faq_plan.a: A life safety survey checks a building against fire and life safety code. The Pennsylvania Department of Health defines it as a survey verifying that a facility provides a reasonable degree of safety through construction, fire protection, egress, and occupancy features. For hospitals, 42 CFR 482.41 says the hospital must meet the applicable provisions of the Life Safety Code, NFPA 101.

faq_plan.q: What are good safety survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Good safety survey questions name one behavior the person has seen for themselves: my supervisor acts on hazards I report, or I have the equipment to do my job safely. Rate each out of 5 and add one open box for the hazard people worry about most. Describe your site and its hazards, and Emergent drafts a first set of these questions for you to edit.

faq_plan.q: Should I start from a safety survey template?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as a starting list, but cut each item that misses your hazards. A template written for offices asks nothing about forklifts or ladders. Templates borrowed from other surveys fit badly too: a 360 survey rates one person from several sides, while a safety survey rates conditions. A survey Emergent builds from your own description starts with your site and its hazards instead.

faq_plan.q: What are some safety survey examples?
faq_plan.a: Beyond the four on this page, other safety survey examples include a lab survey on fume hoods and chemical storage and a contractor survey taken at site check-in. A post-incident survey asks a crew whether a new procedure is workable. Emergent keeps the answers from each one in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do you conduct a safety survey?
faq_plan.ref: how to conduct a safety survey
faq_plan.a: Run it on a fixed schedule, with the people closest to the work. NYSIF guidance has supervisors, safety directors, or safety committee teams make regular, detailed surveys of the workplace. Run the staff version once a year, with a short pulse survey on the weakest items between runs. Keep each one open for 2 weeks across every shift.

faq_plan.q: What is a health and safety survey?
faq_plan.ref: what is a health and safety survey
faq_plan.a: A health and safety survey looks for risks to the people who work at a site, such as blocked exits or lifting strain. The questionnaire version asks staff what they see on their own shifts. Keep it anonymous and short, and break the results out by site or shift so each supervisor gets a list to act on.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits two meanings of safety survey: staff questionnaires (AHRQ patient safety culture, NSC perception surveys, a research instrument, two survey vendors) and walk-through inspections (NYSIF and Pie Insurance loss-control surveys, aviation safety surveys). None shows what happens after an answer comes in. This page covers both meanings: the FAQ defines the inspection kinds searchers ask about (fire, home, life safety, dwelling surveys) and the culture kind, and the tabs show four safety surveys built from a prompt, each sending its result to the one manager who owns it: an anonymous shift survey, a hospital unit report, a site walk on a phone, and a driver question repeated before and after a change. The culture-survey sibling owns general culture; this page owns safety.

On the 6 North hospital unit, 14 of 34 staff (41%) agree that people speak up when they see something that could harm a patient, and the unit manager, Nadia Stanhope, receives a report of only her unit with its three lowest statements.

On a Friday site walk at Pinegrove Avenue, the foreman answers No to guardrails in place on open edges on level 3, item 7 of 15, which opens a task for the superintendent, Owen Lachance, due in 24 hours.

Delivery drivers answer the same time-pressure question each quarter, scoring 2.7 out of 5 in January, and after the fleet manager caps routes at 120 stops, 58 drivers answer in April and the average reaches 3.8.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Safety Survey That Sends Each Manager Their Own Results'; hero 'Build a safety survey that saves every answer by shift or site in a database you own and alerts the manager in charge.' covers the whole job; how-to description one sentence: 'Seven steps to plan a safety survey that people answer honestly and that gives each result a manager who acts on it.'

intent.evidence: Top 10 splits staff perception surveys (AHRQ, NSC) and walk-through inspections (NYSIF, Pie). The page carries both: how-to 01 'A perception survey asks workers how safe they feel... A walkthrough checklist records what a supervisor sees on the floor'; FAQ defines fire, home, life safety and culture of safety surveys; tabs show a perception survey, a unit report, a site walk and a repeated driver question; example statements ('I can stop an unsafe job without getting blamed', 'my supervisor acts on hazards I report').

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'pickers and loaders at the Merced distribution center', 'guardrails are in place on open edges', 'capped routes at 120 stops', 'a group score stays hidden until 5 people in it have answered'. Table generated from the library (QC V2/V3 pass).

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Describe the work and who will answer it.', 'Each answer is saved with the site and shift it came from', 'Every quarter, pickers and loaders...', 'On Fridays, the foreman...'.

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean; sentences short and single-idea, e.g. 'Split it in two.' 'It closes when a recheck answers Yes.'

voice.evidence: Operator detail, no hype: 'He answered No, which opened a task for the superintendent, Owen Lachance, due in 24 hours.' Forced link sentences in FAQ 4, 7 and 10 recorded as a note.

truth.evidence: Emergent claims map to claims_used ids (prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, no-caps, custom-domain 'which Emergent includes and charges in credits', code-export 'On paid plans'). Third-party facts match their domain_sources quotes: Gulf Shores ('slipping, tripping, and cooking', 'written recommendations'), AHRQ ('the extent to which their organizational culture supports patient safety'), 42 CFR 482.41, NYSIF ('supervisors, safety directors, or safety committee teams'), Pew (two quotes), study guide (FAQ 1, 10, attributed 'One firefighter study guide'). Anonymity holds across fields: feature 2 'The survey asks for no name' and stores site and shift; tab 1 'with no name field'; mockup 'Ask for shift and role, never a name'; reminders go to shifts, not people; the named site walk (tab 3) is an inspection, not the anonymous survey. Numbers agree copy to image (2.4/4.1/23/3.0; 14 of 34 = 41%; 2.7 to 3.8, 58).

distinct.evidence: Its own angle (an owner for every result, inspection and perception kinds); no sibling primary in a heading; culture-survey sibling avoided ('Safety Culture' chip and 'culture of safety survey' FAQ sit inside the safety topic).

faq.evidence: 10 Semrush-sourced and secondary questions, all about safety surveys, none naming a brand or file format; each answered in the first sentence ('A life safety survey checks a building against fire and life safety code.'); hub link in item 2; 3 sibling links; secondaries 'safety survey questions', 'safety survey template', 'safety survey examples' carried naturally.
